question: On Passage — Sunshine Protection Act (H R 139)
plain_language: This bill makes daylight saving time the new, permanent standard time. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Lulu’s Law (S 1003)
plain_language: This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission to issue an order explicitly permitting the transmission of wireless emergency alerts to mobile phones in the event of a shark attack. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Kari’s Law Reporting Act (H R 5201)
plain_language: This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission to publish a report on the enforcement of Kari’s Law, which requires multiline telephone systems to be preconfigured to allow users to dial 9-1-1 directly from any phone without dialing any additional code or prefix. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Emergency Reporting Act (H R 5200)
plain_language: This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission to investigate and report on emergency communications outages (e.g., 9-1-1 outages). This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Expediting Federal Broadband Deployment Reviews Act (H R 1681)
bill_title: Expediting Federal Broadband Deployment Reviews Act
plain_language: This bill establishes an interagency strike force to support federal land management agencies' review of requests for communications use authorizations. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.
